def transform(grid):
    """Restore erased cells in a framed, horizontally periodic color field."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] != 0:
                continue
            # Fixed outer background and the 4-colored top/left frame.
            if r < 2 or c < 2:
                out[r][c] = 1
            elif r == 2 or c == 2:
                out[r][c] = 4
            else:
                # Within the colored field, the row pattern repeats every five
                # columns. The erased runs are shorter than the visible spans
                # on either side, so each residue class has surviving samples.
                vals = [grid[r][k] for k in range(w)
                        if k >= 3 and k % 5 == c % 5 and grid[r][k] != 0]
                if not vals:
                    # Fallback: use nearest surviving cell on this row.
                    vals = [grid[r][k] for k in range(w) if k >= 3 and grid[r][k] != 0]
                    k = min((k for k in range(w) if k >= 3 and grid[r][k] != 0),
                            key=lambda k: abs(k-c))
                    out[r][c] = vals[0]
                else:
                    # Mode guards against the short irregular lead-in at the
                    # top of the field; ties resolve by nearest sample.
                    counts = {v: vals.count(v) for v in set(vals)}
                    best = max(counts.values())
                    winners = {v for v, n in counts.items() if n == best}
                    candidates = [k for k in range(w)
                                  if k >= 3 and k % 5 == c % 5
                                  and grid[r][k] in winners]
                    nearest = min(candidates, key=lambda k: abs(k-c))
                    out[r][c] = grid[r][nearest]
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    # Infer the horizontal cycle separately for each patterned row.  The
    # erased rectangles leave enough of the same periodic row visible on both
    # sides; tolerate a few non-periodic seed cells near the left edge.
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] != 0:
                continue
            if r < 2 or c < 2:
                out[r][c] = 1
            elif r == 2 or c == 2:
                out[r][c] = 4
            else:
                known = [(k, grid[r][k]) for k in range(3, w) if grid[r][k] != 0]
                if not known:
                    continue
                def score(p):
                    groups = {}
                    for k, v in known:
                        groups.setdefault(k % p, {}).setdefault(v, 0)
                        groups[k % p][v] += 1
                    # Number of observations explained by the modal color at
                    # each cycle position; smaller periods win equal scores.
                    return sum(max(counts.values()) for counts in groups.values())
                period = max(range(2, 11), key=lambda p: (score(p), -p))
                vals = [v for k, v in known if k % period == c % period]
                if vals:
                    counts = {v: vals.count(v) for v in set(vals)}
                    best = max(counts.values())
                    choices = {v for v, n in counts.items() if n == best}
                    candidates = [(abs(k-c), v) for k, v in known
                                  if k % period == c % period and v in choices]
                    out[r][c] = min(candidates)[1]
    return out
PY

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] != 0:

                out[r][c] = 1
            elif r == 2 or c == 2:
                out[r][c] = 4
            else:
                known = [(k, grid[r][k]) for k in range(3, w) if grid[r][k] != 0]

                # Find the shortest horizontal cycle that explains nearly all
                # visible cells. This ignores occasional irregular lead-in.
                errors = {}
                for p in range(2, 11):
                    groups = {}
                    for k, v in known:
                        groups.setdefault(k % p, {}).setdefault(v, 0)
                        groups[k % p][v] += 1
                    errors[p] = len(known) - sum(max(x.values()) for x in groups.values())
                best_error = min(errors.values())
                eligible = [p for p, e in errors.items() if e <= best_error + 1]
                period = min(eligible)
                vals = [v for k, v in known if k % period == c % period]
                counts = {v: vals.count(v) for v in set(vals)}
                best = max(counts.values())
                winners = {v for v, n in counts.items() if n == best}
